text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- European Commission recommends inviting Estonia to the European Union together with Poland, Hungary, Czech, Cyprus and Slovenia. Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves warned against euphoria saying the real fight for membership will only now begin.
- Two U.S. transport planes brought troops and equipment to the international military exercise Baltic Challenge.
- Collector Mati Zerel who recently bought from the United States the KGB files of two parliament members sold them to an unknown buyer.
- The festival of ancient music opened in Viljandi city for the fifteenth year round.
- Colonies of the poisonous blue algae in the Gulf of Tallinn are the largest in recent years, the environment ministry warned.
- The Estonian delegation will continue talks with the World Trade Organisation in Geneva on July 16-18.
- Estonian basketball player Tiit Sokk has agreed to play in Greek club Saloniki Aris next year. His contract is rumoured to be worth 2.8 million kroons.
- The law that allows privatisation of land according to maps is not effective and causes disputes between landowners, surveyors say.
- Tallinn Airport increased its sales in 1996 by a quarter.
